sentences.text: Hybodus possessed two dorsal fins, one of which featured a bony plate likely used for defense.
The shark had two distinct tooth types: sharper ones for catching slippery prey and flatter ones to crush shelled animals.
Males carried specialized organs called pterigopodia that inserted sperm directly into the female during mating.
A preserved specimen of Hybodus hauffianus was discovered containing over 100 belemnite rostra in its stomach.
Hybodus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
It belongs to the family Hybodontidae and the parent group Hybodontinae.

Several species previously assigned to Hybodus from the Cretaceous have been transferred to the genus Meristodonoides, while some Triassic species are not hybodonts and belong to the order Synechodontiformes.
The Paleobiology Database records Hybodus occurrences from the Gzhelian to the Maastrichtian, spanning 303.7 to 66 million years ago.
Specific species like H. reticulatus and H. hauffianus are known from the Early Jurassic of Europe.
With current knowledge, Hybodus is considered endemic to the Jurassic period.
